questions.q: What does revaluation restate, and at what level?
options: Every individual journal line ever posted, regardless of currency
Foreign-currency-denominated balance sheet account balances, at the account balance level, to current period-end rates
Only income statement accounts, to historical rates
The chart of accounts structure itself
questions.explain: Revaluation operates on balance sheet account balances carrying a foreign-currency exposure, restating them to the period-end rate, not on individual transactions.

questions.q: Why doesn't revaluation touch income statement accounts?
options: Because income statement accounts never have foreign currency activity
Because income statement accounts are always in the functional currency already
Because an expense recognized in a given period is historical, and restating it would misstate that period's actual results
Because revaluation is only allowed on asset accounts
questions.explain: Income statement activity reflects what happened at the time; restating it after the fact would distort the period's reported results.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation example, the GBP invoice was originally accounted at $10,795.00 and revalues to $11,135.00 at period end. What does this produce?
options: A realized gain of $340.00
A permanent write-off of the invoice
No journal entry at all
An unrealized loss of $340.00
questions.explain: Since the USD value of the liability increased, this is an unrealized loss of $340.00, booked as a temporary revaluation journal.

questions.q: What typically happens to a revaluation journal in the following period?
options: It stays on the books permanently
It gets converted into a budget entry
It automatically reverses, since it is a temporary adjustment to a still-open, point-in-time balance
It is deleted without a trace
questions.explain: Revaluation journals are typically set to auto-reverse the next period, because they estimate current value of an open balance rather than permanently restating it.

questions.q: Why must revaluation run before translation each period?
options: Translation always runs automatically before any journals post
A ledger's own foreign-currency exposure must be correctly reflected before that ledger's balances are translated into another currency for group reporting
Translation and revaluation are unrelated and order doesn't matter
Revaluation is only needed once a year, at year-end
questions.explain: Revaluation corrects the ledger's own balances first; translation then restates the whole corrected ledger into a different reporting currency for consolidation.
